text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 each ran exactly once per case: they appeared in all 200 traces, averaged about 1 occurrence per trace, and repeats were virtually absent. In the later window, each of the five averages about 3 occurrences per trace, and repeated executions within a case appear in about 67 in 100 traces, while participation remains complete. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- The strict sequence through these activities dissolved: A30 preceded A31 in about 97 in 100 earlier traces but only about 33 in 100 later traces; A14 preceded A30 in about 98 in 100 earlier traces but about 33 in 100 later; A36 preceded A46 in all earlier traces but about 33 in 100 later. In the later window these pairs are mostly interleaved or repeated (about 67 in 100). [REL014, REL034, REL053]
- A38's dominant successor changed: before, about 99 in 100 of A38's outgoing transitions went to A25; in the later window about 66 in 100 go to A30 and about 32 in 100 to A25. [DIR007]
- Repeats at a distance are new: A30→A30 and A31→A31 repetitions were seen in only 1 earlier trace each but in about 128 and 116 later traces, typically 4–5 positions apart, and pairs among A31, A36 and A37 that were usually 1–2 positions apart are now spread over 1–5; the five activities' positions also spread out (A30's upper-quartile position rose from about 0.40 to about 0.53). [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, POS006, POS010]
- A10 became rare: it appeared in about 71 in 100 earlier traces but only about 25 in 100 later traces, and its typical position moved from about 0.85 to about 0.48 of the trace length. It now rarely runs with the main line — with A30, co-occurrence fell from about 71 in 100 to 25 in 100, with A30 appearing without A10 in 75 in 100 later traces — A10 preceding A46 fell from about 65 in 100 to about 19 in 100, A10 within five steps after A44 dropped from about 139 traces to about 14, and A10's own outgoing transitions, previously almost all to A45, are now spread across many targets. [OCC005, POS001, REL005, REL012, LAG013, DIR004]
- A44's routing flipped: before, about 72 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A10 and about 27 in 100 to A45; in the later window about 80 in 100 go to A45 and only about 5 in 100 to A10. [DIR008]
- The rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A08 now participate about two to three times as often, from roughly 5–9 in 100 traces to roughly 18–26 in 100 (resting on 9–18 traces before and 35–51 after), and A14, A15 and A46 now occasionally lead into them. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR009]
- Smaller shifts: A22 and A28 occur slightly later in the trace than before, and A22's coupling with A10 weakened (co-occurrence about 41 in 100 to about 13 in 100). [POS004, POS005, REL003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment formed by A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 — previously executed exactly once per case in a fixed order — is now repeated about three times per case in roughly two thirds of traces, with A38 typically looping back to A30 rather than exiting to A25. Screening qualified 114 control-flow items where only about 1 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the volume of agreeing evidence cannot be a sampling artefact. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR007, screening]

The support is direct and consistent: all five activities tripled their per-case frequency while still running in every trace; their fixed pairwise orders gave way to interleaved or repeated execution; A38→A30 became A38's dominant outgoing transition; and self-repetitions of A30 and A31, virtually absent before, now occur in about two thirds of traces at 4–5 position lags. [REL014, REL034, REL053, LAG002, LAG004]

Limitations: the evidence shows the multiplied occurrences and the redirected A38 exit but cannot establish the exact loop body — whether all five activities repeat together in every cycle or some are skipped in some cycles — and position and lag measures count steps between events, not clock time. A competing reading that cannot be fully ruled out is a reordering of independent executions without repetition, though the tripled per-case counts and the new A38→A30 dominance make repetition the more direct interpretation; likewise, whether A10's decline is an independent routing change or a side effect of the repeated segment cannot be determined from these windows. [OCC006, DIR007, LAG002, OCC005]

Other differences: A10 is now executed in far fewer cases (about 25 in 100 traces, down from about 71) and has lost its place between A44/A45 and A46/A47, with A44 now usually followed by A45 instead of A10; the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A08 participate about two to three times as often as before; and A22 and A28 occur slightly later. These differences are reported separately and are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC005, REL005, REL012, DIR008, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS004, POS005]
